metadata.title: Red Runaways: Hypervelocity Stars, Hills Ejecta and Other Outliers in the F-M Star Regime

evidence.quote:
We identify hypervelocity stars as stars whose current
kinetic energy is greater than the gravitational potential
(described in Section 2.2) at their position.

We construct a catalog of objects which satisfy this
criterion and present a subset of them in Table 2.

retain only the candidates that pass our strict proper motion quality cuts

Of our
7 strong candidates, two of four are found to intersect
the Galactic plane at positions coincident with spiral

notes: J082015.88+362223.26, J160707.30+372350.97, J131238.82+393312.13, J175010.68+262448.38, J075516.37+662909.15, J024605.10+312254.29, and J093103.04+134728.81 are the seven strict Table 2 entries selected by the paper’s explicit present-day escape criterion (current kinetic energy greater than the gravitational potential; T:p8-b10, T:p9-b0) and retained as “7 strong candidates” (T:p13-b2). J082015.88+362223.26, J075516.37+662909.15, and J024605.10+312254.29 are marked “Infalling” in Table 2 and are the three called “unbound, infalling, high metallicity stars” in the Figure 8 material (T:p10-b0; I:p10-b0), so their infalling status does not remove them. Section 4.2.1 says these candidates have a greater than 60% chance of being hypervelocity stars even though none is unbound at more than 2σ (T:p10-b5). The 35 escape-criterion objects mentioned only as an online table without individual names (T:p8-b16) cannot be rostered. J135855.65+552538.19 and the other Table 3 Hills candidates (T:p11-b1; selection described at T:p12-b1) are not included: the paper selects them by central-region crossing/ejection speed, which is a proposed origin/ejection criterion rather than an explicit present-day Galactic escape or unbound criterion; even J135855.65+552538.19 is called the best Hills-origin candidate, not explicitly Galactic unbound. The literature Hills stars compared in Figure 9 (T:p11-b0; I:p11-b0) are not individually identified in the supplied material. The statement that seven Palladino et al. candidates are rediscovered (T:p8-b16) does not map those prior candidates to specific Table 2 names in the supplied text, so the Table 2 stars are recorded under this paper’s own candidates_found criterion rather than as individually supported follow_up.

J082015.88+362223.26: The target J082015.88+362223.26 is the first entry of Table 2 (I:p9-b0). The table reports only the total proper-motion magnitude (24.27 mas/yr), not separate R.A. and Dec. components, so no proper_motion_ra/proper_motion_dec values are extracted. No distance, parallax, radial velocity, or galactocentric radius is reported individually for this star. The R.A. and Dec. values are interpreted from the standard J2000 IAU designation because no separate coordinate columns are given. The >60% unbound probability is a group statement explicitly applied to all seven Table 2 candidates, not a separately tabulated value for this star; the paper also states that none have more than a 2σ chance of being unbound.

J160707.30+372350.97: Table 2 gives only the total proper-motion magnitude, not separate equatorial proper-motion components. No radial velocity, parallax, distance, galactocentric radius, or individual bound/unbound probability is reported for this star. The RA and Dec are read directly from the IAU designation rather than converted to decimal degrees. V_Total is interpreted as the total space velocity in the paper's Galactocentric right-handed frame (see T:p3-b10 and T:p3-b11); Table 2 identifies it for a hypervelocity candidate.

J131238.82+393312.13: Target J131238.82+393312.13 appears in Table 2 (T:p9-b0; I:p9-b0). Its RA and Dec are transcribed from the IAU designation. The paper reports only total proper motion, not separate equatorial proper-motion components, and does not provide a distance or parallax for this star. The >60% unbound/hypervelocity probability is a group statement for all seven Table 2 candidates; the same passage also states none has more than a 2σ chance of being unbound, which appears to refer to statistical significance (T:p10-b5).

J175010.68+262448.38: J175010.68+262448.38 appears in Table 2 (T:p9-b0, I:p9-b0), which provides a total proper-motion magnitude rather than separate R.A./Dec. proper-motion components, so no proper-motion component values are recorded. No individual parallax, distance, or radial velocity is tabulated for this star. The R.A. and Dec. are read from the IAU designation; no separate coordinate columns are given. The >60% statement at T:p10-b5 applies collectively to all Table 2 candidates and is phrased as the chance of being a hypervelocity star; it is recorded as a lower bound on unbound probability because the paper defines hypervelocity as escape-potential speed.

J075516.37+662909.15: RA and Dec are taken from the target's IAU identifier in Table 2 (T:p9-b0). The Table 2 row reports a total proper motion (8.95 mas yr−1) and its uncertainty, not separate RA/Dec proper-motion components, so no component proper motions are recorded. No parallax, distance, radial velocity, or galactocentric radius is reported for this target. The >60% statement at T:p10-b5 is applied collectively to all seven strong hypervelocity candidates and is recorded as a lower bound on unbound probability.

J024605.10+312254.29: The Table 2 row at T:p9-b0 reports only total proper motion (11.0 mas/yr) and its error (4.94 mas/yr), not separate R.A. and Dec. proper-motion components, so no proper_motion_ra or proper_motion_dec values are assigned. The materials do not report a distance, parallax, radial velocity, current galactocentric radius, or individual bound/unbound probability for J024605.10+312254.29. The R.A. and Dec. values are inferred from the IAU-style identifier; the table itself does not print separate coordinate columns.

J093103.04+134728.81: Target J093103.04+134728.81 appears only in Table 2 (T:p9-b0; I:p9-b0). The table does not separately report right ascension, declination, parallax/distance, radial velocity, or individual proper-motion components; its total proper motion and error cannot be assigned to the equatorial proper-motion components. V_Total is treated as the Galactic-rest-frame total speed because the paper selects hypervelocity stars by comparing current kinetic energy with the Galactic potential and lists V_esc alongside it. The >60% statement in T:p10-b5 is explicitly a group statement for all seven Table 2 candidates. The same passage's phrase "more than a 2σ chance of being unbound" is internally ambiguous in context, so only the explicit >60% hypervelocity lower bound is recorded; the definition of hypervelocity is given in T:p2-b6.
